claims.text: A mild post-deposition anneal at approximately 300 °C is an applicable treatment for the FeNiCrCoCu coating.
Mild post-deposition annealing promotes Cu surface segregation in FeNiCrCoCu coatings.
Annealing and subsequent high-temperature sliding cause segregated Cu to oxidize in situ.
The treatment forms a continuous nanocrystalline Cu oxide layer at the coating surface and along grain boundaries.
The Cu oxide layer is adherent to the coating.
The Cu oxide layer acts as a protective barrier during high-temperature sliding.
The Cu oxide layer reduces local stress concentrations.
The treatment shifts microscopic deformation from intragranular dislocation glide to grain-boundary-mediated sliding.
At approximately 300 °C, tribochemical reactions are active in the FeNiCrCoCu sliding contact.
Approximately 300 °C is a relevant elevated-temperature sliding-test regime for an annealed HEA coating.
Compared with the as-deposited coating, the annealed coating will have a lower wear rate during sliding at approximately 300 °C.
Compared with the as-deposited coating, the annealed coating will have a lower coefficient of friction during sliding at approximately 300 °C.
The annealed coating will exhibit less microscopic plastic deformation than the as-deposited coating.
The annealed coating will show fewer dislocation-related features and more grain-boundary-sliding signatures.
At temperatures significantly above 300 °C, additional wear mechanisms may alter the predicted behavior.
The kinetics of Cu segregation and oxide formation in this coating remain unquantified.
The critical annealing parameters required to create an optimal Cu oxide layer remain unquantified.
The durability of the proposed oxide layer under prolonged sliding and cyclic thermal loading remains unquantified.
